title: Monomial quotients are Tor independent over a log regular chart
statement:
Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian log regular fs log scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] and let $\bar s$ be a geometric point. Let $A=\mathcal O_{S,\bar s}$ be its strict local ring (the stalk of the etale structure sheaf [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]). Let $Q\to M_S$ be a chart inducing an isomorphism $Q\cong\overline M_{S,\bar s}$, with $Q$ sharp fs. Let $\Lambda$ be a localization of $\mathbf Z[1/N,\zeta_N]$, for an integer $N$ invertible in $A$ and a chosen primitive $N$th root of unity in $A$, giving $A$ a $\Lambda$-algebra structure. Let $P$ be an fs monoid and $\gamma:Q\to P$ a homomorphism with injective group completion and finite torsion subgroup of its cokernel of order invertible in $A$. Set $R=\Lambda[P]$, $C=\Lambda[Q]$, and $B=A\otimes_C R$. These monoid rings have basis $z^p$, with $z^pz^{p'}=z^{p+p'}$.

For every monoid ideal $J\subseteq P$ (a subset satisfying $J+P\subseteq J$, including the empty subset), let $(J)\subseteq R$ be generated by its monomials. Then, for every $i>0$,
$$\operatorname{Tor}^{C}_i(A,R/(J))=0,\qquad \operatorname{Tor}^{R}_i(B,R/(J))=0.$$
The Tor functors are [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. The same vanishings hold after adjoining finitely many polynomial variables to $R$ and $B$ and additionally killing any subset of those variables in the second argument: if $R'=R[y_1,\ldots,y_s]$, $B'=A\otimes_C R'$, and $K=(J,y_j:j\in L)$ for $L\subseteq\{1,\ldots,s\}$, then $\operatorname{Tor}^{C}_i(A,R'/K)=\operatorname{Tor}^{R'}_i(B',R'/K)=0$ for all $i>0$.

proof.text: Put $D=\mathbf Z[Q]$. The ring $A=\mathcal O_{S,\bar s}$ of the statement is the colimit of $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ over all pointed etale neighbourhoods $(V,\bar v)$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]; this filtered colimit of rings is computed on underlying sets. The affine pointed neighbourhoods form an initial full subcategory [lemma-weil-pbc-affine-neighbourhood-cofinal], so restricting the colimit to them, and then to the chosen representatives, is a canonical isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-initial-full-subcategory] onto the ring $\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{S,\bar s}$ of [lem-trf-kato-tor-independence-chart], since $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)=A_V$ for $V=\operatorname{Spec}A_V$. It commutes with the coprojections, hence with the maps from $\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)$ through which the chart $Q\to\Gamma(S,M_S)\to(A,\cdot)$ and the $\Lambda$-structure factor. Taking the pointed neighbourhood $(S,\bar s)$ itself, the strict local ring and the characteristic-identifying chart in the statement then satisfy exactly the hypotheses of [lem-trf-kato-tor-independence-chart], with that node's monoid denoted here by $Q$. It gives $\operatorname{Tor}^D_1(D/\mathbf Z[I],A)=0$ for every monoid ideal $I\subseteq Q$. The symmetry isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-tor-symmetry] gives $\operatorname{Tor}^D_1(A,D/\mathbf Z[I])=0$. No ordinary flatness of $D\to A$ is asserted or used.

source.place: Expose X 1.3(vii), printed p.140; Expose VIII 3.5, printed p.115, base-chart monomial ideal test.

proof.text: Treat both assertions together. In the first case put $E=P$ and $H=J$. For the polynomial assertion put $E=P\oplus\mathbf N^s$ and let $H\subseteq E$ consist of $(p,e)$ with either $p\in J$ or $e_j>0$ for some $j\in L$. In both cases $E$ is integral, so it embeds into $G=E^{\rm gp}$; the homomorphism $Q\to E\to G$, $q\mapsto(\gamma(q),0)$ in the second case, is injective by the hypothesis on $\gamma^{\rm gp}$. Both $E$ and $H$ are stable under addition by $Q$. Apply [lem-per-monomial-module-tor-devissage] with $M=A$, $T=E$, $U=H$, using Step 1. With $V_{\mathbf Z}=\mathbf Z[E]/\mathbf Z[H]$ it gives $\operatorname{Tor}^D_i(A,V_{\mathbf Z})=0$ for all $i>0$. Apply it also with $U=\varnothing$ to get the same vanishing for $\mathbf Z[E]$. These applications allow $H=\varnothing$ and $H=E$.

source.place: Expose X 1.3(vii), printed p.140, and Lemma 1.5, printed pp.141--142; agent monomial-module devissage makes the extension from the base-chart ideal test explicit.

proof.text: The ring $\mathbf Z[1/N,\zeta_N]$ embeds into the characteristic-zero field $\mathbf Q(\zeta_N)$; its localization $\Lambda$ is either zero or embeds into that field as well. Thus $\Lambda$ is torsion free over $\mathbf Z$, including the zero-ring case, and is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-pid-torsion-free-module-flat]. To see explicitly the effect of coefficients, let $F_\bullet\to V_{\mathbf Z}$ be a $D$-free resolution [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. Tensoring its augmented sequence over $\mathbf Z$ with $\Lambda$ preserves exactness by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]. Each $\Lambda\otimes_{\mathbf Z}F_n$ is free over $C=\Lambda[Q]$, so this is a $C$-free resolution of $V=\Lambda[E]/(H)$. Termwise $A\otimes_C(\Lambda\otimes_{\mathbf Z}F_n)\cong A\otimes_DF_n$, by $(a\otimes(\lambda\otimes f))\mapsto\lambda a\otimes f$, with inverse $a\otimes f\mapsto a\otimes(1\otimes f)$. The maps commute with the differentials, being induced by the same maps of $F_\bullet$. Tor symmetry [lem-weil-pbc-tor-symmetry] and Step 2 now give $\operatorname{Tor}^C_i(A,V)=0$ for $i>0$. The identical argument for $\mathbf Z[E]$ gives $\operatorname{Tor}^C_i(A,\Lambda[E])=0$.

source.place: Tag 00LY (section-tor), Tag 00HD (lemma-flat), and More on Algebra Tag 0AUW (lemma-dedekind-torsion-free-flat); free-resolution calculation for the coefficient extension.

proof.text: Write $R_E=\Lambda[E]$ and $B_E=A\otimes_C R_E$. Choose a $C$-free resolution $G_\bullet\to A$ [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. By the last vanishing of Step 3, $G_\bullet\otimes_C R_E\to B_E$ is exact in positive degrees, and its degree-zero homology is $B_E$. Each term is $R_E$-free, so it is an $R_E$-free resolution of $B_E$. For $V=R_E/(H)$, its tensor with $V$ is termwise the same complex as $G_\bullet\otimes_C V$, by $(g\otimes r)\otimes v\mapsto g\otimes rv$, with inverse $g\otimes v\mapsto(g\otimes1)\otimes v$. Hence its positive homology is $\operatorname{Tor}^C_i(A,V)=0$ by Step 3, proving $\operatorname{Tor}^{R_E}_i(B_E,V)=0$. For $E=P$ this is the second displayed vanishing. For $E=P\oplus\mathbf N^s$, the basis bijection $z^{(p,e)}\mapsto z^p y^e$ identifies $R_E$ with $R'$ and $(H)$ with $K$; indeed $H$ is precisely the monomial basis set of $(J,y_j:j\in L)$. It identifies $B_E$ with $B'$ as well. Thus the same computations give both polynomial vanishings, including $s=0$, $L=\varnothing$, and all variables killed.
